title: Upper limb midterm · 14 May 2025
note: Cover labels this a TUMS upper-limb midterm, 14 May 2025. 25 questions with photographed key; retained as an optional supplement, not relabeled as a final.

questions.prompt: The floor of the anatomical snuffbox includes:
questions.note: Scaphoid and trapezium form the bony floor.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: The lateral cord receives contributions from:
questions.note: Anterior divisions of upper and middle trunks contribute C5–7.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All connect the upper limb to the thoracic wall EXCEPT:
questions.note: Teres major connects scapula to humerus.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Thoracoacromial artery arises from:
questions.note: It is a second-part axillary branch.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All are related to surgical neck of humerus EXCEPT:
questions.note: Profunda brachii accompanies radial nerve in the radial groove.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which muscle can compensate for loss of supinator?
questions.note: Biceps is a powerful supinator, especially with elbow flexed.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: A branch of the lateral cord is:
questions.note: Musculocutaneous is the terminal lateral-cord branch.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which medial-cord statement is false?
options: It gives rise to ulnar nerve
It supplies a pectoralis minor branch
questions.note: The typical medial cord carries C8–T1, not C5.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which is not a branch of radial artery?
questions.note: Interosseous recurrent usually arises from posterior interosseous artery.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Quadrangular-space boundaries include all EXCEPT:
questions.note: Long head of triceps, not biceps, forms its medial border.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which listed muscle or group adducts and medially rotates the arm?
options: Latissimus dorsi, pectoralis major and infraspinatus
Latissimus dorsi, pectoralis major, subscapularis and teres minor
questions.note: Other choices include a lateral rotator (infraspinatus or teres minor).
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: In injury to the lower anterior arm, all these muscles may be paralyzed EXCEPT:
questions.note: EPL is a posterior-compartment radial/posterior-interosseous muscle. The source implies anterior nerves; exact lesion anatomy is underspecified.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which muscle originates from radius?
questions.note: FPL originates on anterior radius; EPL originates on ulna.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which tendon passes within the shoulder joint capsule?
questions.note: Long biceps tendon is intracapsular but extrasynovial.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Most lymph from the upper lateral breast first reaches which axillary group?
questions.note: Pectoral/anterior nodes receive most lateral breast drainage.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Carpal tunnel contains all EXCEPT:
questions.note: FCU inserts into pisiform outside the tunnel.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which statement about FDP is false?
options: It takes the common flexor origin
It gives origin to four lumbricals
It receives anterior interosseous and ulnar supply
questions.note: FDP originates mainly on ulna and interosseous membrane, not the common flexor origin.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which innervation is incorrect?
questions.note: Lumbricals 1–2 are median and 3–4 ulnar supplied.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: At the wrist, ulnar artery is:
questions.note: Ulnar artery lies radial/lateral to the nerve in Guyon canal.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which tendons attach directly to index-finger phalanges?
options: Extensor digitorum, lumbricals and extensor indicis
Extensor digitorum, dorsal interossei, lumbricals and extensor indicis
questions.note: ED has central/terminal bony slips. EI and lumbricals insert into the extensor expansion, not independent direct phalangeal insertions. The source question omits long flexor attachments and is limited to the listed extensor combinations.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Nerves responsible for wrist abduction are:
questions.note: Radial wrist extensors and median-supplied FCR cooperate in radial deviation.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which muscles attach to coracoid process?
questions.note: Short biceps, coracobrachialis and pectoralis minor attach to coracoid.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which joint classification is correct?
questions.note: First CMC is saddle; IP joints are hinges.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Upper lateral cutaneous nerve of arm arises from:
questions.note: It is a cutaneous branch of axillary nerve.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which muscles insert on first metacarpal?
options: Abductor pollicis brevis and opponens pollicis
Abductor pollicis brevis and flexor pollicis brevis
Abductor pollicis longus and flexor pollicis brevis
Abductor pollicis longus and opponens pollicis
questions.note: APL inserts on the base and opponens on the shaft; APB/FPB principally attach to proximal phalanx.
questions.subject: anatomy

audit.method: Source photograph transcription; anatomy review; original defects preserved, multiple defensible choices accepted.
